title: The Gap
summary: The Gap is Dylan's in-world build space: a place to adjust combat tools, develop Talents, craft Artifacts and test a loadout away from an encounter.
imageAlt: The Gap, a dark interior used for Dylan's build management

facts.label: Access
facts.value: Outside combat; fast travel described by Remedy

sections.heading: What can you do in the Gap?
paragraphs: Remedy describes the Gap as a space within Dylan's mind rather than an ordinary inventory screen. Weapon Forms, supernatural Combat Abilities and Talents are managed here. A September developer briefing also says players can craft Artifacts and test builds in the Gap.

The practical distinction is between collecting a possibility in Manhattan and making it part of a build. Finding an Untapped Artifact is not the same thing as equipping a finished Artifact: the crafting step belongs in the Gap.

sections.heading: When should you return?
paragraphs: The official combat explanation places Gap access outside combat. Once a new Form, boss-granted ability, Talent or Untapped Artifact is available, review the combination before judging it in the next encounter. Remedy says travel between Manhattan's Zones and the Gap is near-instantaneous, but has not published a full list of every access point.

Do not read preview menu images as a complete launch inventory. The first run deliberately limits some choices; New Game Plus expands Talent options, Combat Ability combinations and Artifact capacity.

playerTakeaway: We use the Gap as a comparison and testing stop between encounters. Keep an unlocked option, a crafted Artifact and an equipped slot separate when you read a build.

title: FBC Field Office
summary: The Federal Bureau of Control's field office is the evolving central hub linking the game's handcrafted Manhattan Zones; it is not a claim that the city is one seamless open-world map.
imageAlt: Manhattan zone artwork; the field office itself is not identified in this image

facts.label: Map structure
facts.value: Zone-based, not a seamless open world

sections.heading: How is Manhattan connected?
paragraphs: In a developer-commented Xbox presentation, the city's major Zones branch from a central area containing the FBC field office. The office is described as an evolving hub. That gives players a better mental model than treating every distorted street as one continuous map.

Each Zone is intended to have a distinct appearance, encounters, lore and discoveries. The office connects that structure, while the Gap serves the separate purpose of shaping Dylan's build. The two should not be confused just because both are places a player may revisit.

sections.heading: What is not mapped yet?
paragraphs: We have not found a complete office floor plan, every Zone entrance or a fixed order for all routes. For now, we explain what the hub does instead of inventing corridors, vendors or fast-travel markers.
For navigation, follow the currently available Zone and story objective. For equipment choices, use the Gap; for a specific previewed traversal challenge, see the Metro Fault file.

playerTakeaway: Our simplest map is: the field office connects Zones, the Gap handles the build, and the Oldest House remains its own story location.

title: Aberrant Forms Compared
summary: Six named early weapon choices divide into Primary and Secondary Forms. They change the speed, reach and target pattern of Dylan's transforming Aberrant rather than representing six separate loot drops.
imageAlt: Aberrant scythe form shown in gameplay artwork

comparison.heading: Six previewed Forms at a glance
comparison.introduction: These roles come from a first-party hands-on of the opening hour. They are tactical descriptions, not a final damage ranking or full unlock list.
rows: Fast, close-range attacks; boosted critical chance
High single-target damage; bonus from behind
Extra reach for a melee setup

sections.heading: How do the Form pools work?
paragraphs: The Xbox hands-on describes an early choice among Flurry, Slash and Slice, followed later in the preview by a choice among Crush, Drill and Extend. A separate Combo Ender pool supplies finishers. These pools let Dylan combine different attack roles within a single Aberrant loadout.
The previewer notes that other Forms can eventually be unlocked. That observation does not establish an exact unlock order, upgrade cost, complete Form count or a permanent lockout.

sections.heading: How should you choose an opening pair?
paragraphs: A close-range Primary Form and a reach-oriented Secondary Form cover different problems; a wide Primary Form and a heavy Secondary Form lean toward crowd pressure and impact. That is how we read the roles shown so far, not a tested best-in-slot ranking.

Watch what a fight asks of you—single target, group control, reach or sustained pressure—before treating one weapon animation as universally strongest. Talents, abilities and Artifacts may alter that judgment in the finished game.

playerTakeaway: We compare Forms by role first. We do not have reliable retail damage values, full upgrade trees or a complete Combo Ender list yet.

title: Combat Abilities Compared
summary: Barrage, Seekers and Shield were presented as choices after an early Resonant encounter; their known functions point to different ways to regain control of a fight.
imageAlt: Combat Ability selection shown in preview material

facts.label: Resource loop
facts.value: Melee hits restore Combat Ability resource

facts.label: First-run limitation
facts.value: Some boss choices are exclusive until later runs

comparison.heading: Three early choices shown
comparison.introduction: A hands-on preview describes these as an early choice, not a complete list of launch abilities or a measured tier list.
rows: Raises floating rocks and supports a ram

sections.heading: Why does the choice matter?
paragraphs: Remedy says powerful Resonants grant supernatural Combat Abilities and that some rewards branch into different playstyles. The opening hands-on identifies Barrage, Seekers and Shield after an early boss. A player choosing among them is choosing a role, not simply a different visual effect.

Melee hits restore the resource used by Combat Abilities. Abilities can stun enemies, enabling executions that temporarily raise melee damage. This loop explains why a defensive or summoning option can still support aggressive Aberrant play.

sections.heading: What changes in New Game Plus?
paragraphs: The developer's NG+ explanation says multiple different Combat Abilities from the same boss can be equipped in a later run. It does not establish that every first-run branch is available immediately, or that the opening choice has no consequence.
Mold Turrets are a separate example of a tactical summon described by Remedy. Do not merge them with Seekers or count them as a named opening reward without a direct announcement.

playerTakeaway: We would choose by the problem the ability solves—distance, independent pressure or protection—while keeping the Aberrant resource loop in mind.

title: Artifacts and Crafting
summary: Artifacts are passive equipment crafted from Untapped Artifacts in the Gap. The known first-run limit is three equipped slots; New Game Plus opens a fourth.
imageAlt: The Gap, where Artifacts can be crafted from Untapped Artifacts

facts.label: Material
facts.value: Untapped Artifacts found in the world

facts.label: Equip slots
facts.value: Three in first run; four in NG+

comparison.heading: Do not confuse these states
comparison.introduction: The acquisition and equipment steps are distinct. The numbers below describe slots, not the total number of Artifacts in the game.
rows: A crafted item assigned to a slot
Compare it with the rest of the build

sections.heading: What can an Artifact change?
paragraphs: Remedy describes passive effects covering survival, combat, exploration and resources. Some modifiers have conditions or trade-offs, so the highest-looking bonus is not automatically the best fit for every fight.

The official explanation gives a three-slot limit on a first playthrough and a fourth slot in New Game Plus. It does not provide a complete catalog of effects, crafting costs or acquisition locations.

sections.heading: How should you evaluate one?
paragraphs: Start with the build's weakness. A modifier that helps resource recovery serves a different purpose from one that improves survival. Check whether the effect requires a condition you can reliably trigger with your chosen Forms and Combat Abilities.

A preorder or edition-linked Artifact is a specific entitlement, not evidence that every Artifact is sold separately or that the full crafting system is bypassed. Keep edition contents and in-game discoveries separate.

playerTakeaway: Before we rank an Artifact, we want its effect and trigger condition. The three-versus-four figure tells us the equip limit, not the collectible count.

title: New Game Plus
summary: NG+ carries much of Dylan's combat progression into a fresh run while story-gated traversal abilities reset. It also broadens Talent, ability and Artifact combinations.
imageAlt: CONTROL Resonant Talent interface from preview imagery

facts.label: Carries over
facts.value: Aberrant upgrades, health and ability-resource upgrades, Combat Abilities, Talents, Artifacts

facts.label: New flexibility
facts.value: Additional Talent nodes and same-boss ability combinations

comparison.heading: What follows Dylan into NG+?
comparison.introduction: This is the developer's announced carry-over policy, not a claim about every inventory item or activity flag.
rows: Unlocks persist; additional combinations become possible

sections.heading: Why is the second run different?
paragraphs: Remedy says a first playthrough cannot unlock everything. NG+ allows new Talent nodes and combinations of different Combat Abilities gained from the same boss. That makes it a build-experiment run, not merely the same campaign with bigger numbers.
The world also pushes back: enemies and encounters evolve, and some bosses may have new behaviors. The announcement does not provide a fixed level scaling formula or list every modified encounter.

sections.heading: What needs to be reacquired?
paragraphs: Traversal abilities remain tied to the story and do not carry over. That is different from supernatural Combat Abilities, which are explicitly part of the retained progression. Plan exploration around renewed route gates even if your combat build is already developed.

World Quests, bounties, collectibles and alternative side-story outcomes are reasons Remedy gives for returning. Their exact reset states and reward lists should be verified against the released game before a completion checklist is published.

playerTakeaway: We would keep build notes for NG+, but we would not expect old traversal shortcuts to stay open at the start of the new story.

title: First Resonant Entity
summary: An opening-hours hands-on describes a giant partial head embedded in the street, using telekinetic debris. It is a preview encounter, not a confirmed final boss name.
imageAlt: Promotional Resonant encounter artwork; not an identification of the previewed boss

facts.label: Shown threat
facts.value: Telekinetic debris and a large embedded head

sections.heading: What did the hands-on actually show?
paragraphs: A first-party Xbox hands-on follows Dylan from the Oldest House into Manhattan and describes an early Resonant Entity as a large, partly embedded head. The encounter uses telekinetic debris. The previewer also sees the entity clearing Hiss from its surroundings, which distinguishes it from an ordinary Hiss enemy.

The report presents Barrage, Seekers and Shield as the supernatural ability options following this encounter. It does not publish a retail boss name, health value, elemental resistance or a guaranteed step-by-step pattern.

sections.heading: How should players read the preview?
paragraphs: Treat the encounter as an introduction to what a Resonant can change in a build. Remedy says major Resonants are story-integrated bosses that grant Combat Abilities, sometimes with branching choices.

The separately previewed Central Resonant has fire and magma hazards. The two should not be merged into one entry merely because both are Resonants. A final retail boss route will need gameplay verification.

playerTakeaway: We expect a boss-linked ability decision here, but we are not building a strategy around an unconfirmed name or pre-release damage values.

title: World Quests and Faults
summary: World Quests are self-contained narrative stories. Faults are a distinct activity type; Metro Fault is a named preview route, not proof of a complete published Fault list.
imageAlt: Warped transit space used to illustrate a previewed Fault route

comparison.heading: Which kind of objective is this?
comparison.introduction: These are categories disclosed by Remedy and preview materials, not a complete quest log.
rows: A full chapter and mission order
All quest names, choices and rewards
Total count and full route map

sections.heading: What does the mission structure tell us?
paragraphs: Remedy identifies two primary narrative quest types: Dylan's Journey and World Quests. Zones also contain combat encounters, environmental challenges, hidden discoveries and optional activities. The stated design is exploration on the player's terms rather than clearing an icon-filled map.

A category name is not a mission title. Do not mistake the public term World Quest for a verified list of individual side missions. The known Metro Fault is a concrete preview route and belongs under the broader activity discussion.

sections.heading: How should you plan a route before launch?
paragraphs: Use the main campaign for story progression and treat Zone activities as opportunities to gain context or test movement and combat. A preview of Metro Fault shows a traversal-focused space and the Reach reward, but does not establish that all Faults use the same objective pattern.

New Game Plus is expected to offer reasons to revisit missed World Quests, bounties and collectibles. Until the released quest log can be checked, no page here assigns fictional task steps or completion percentages.

playerTakeaway: We use these activity types to decide what to follow next. Exact routes and reward checklists can wait until we can verify the retail game.
